about.title: Personal Injury Help in Rancho Palos Verdes, California
about.longDescription: Rancho Palos Verdes sits along the coast in Los Angeles County, with traffic moving through corridors like Palos Verdes Drive S, Hawthorne Boulevard, and Western Avenue. In the most recent full year on record, the city logged 33 injury collisions and 43 people injured, with no traffic deaths reported. Collisions tend to cluster on Monday afternoons between 2 and 4 p.m., a pattern likely tied to commute and school pickup traffic converging on these same routes. If you were hurt in a crash, a slip-and-fall, or another type of accident in Rancho Palos Verdes, sorting out medical bills, lost income, and insurance calls can feel like a full-time job on top of recovering. LawProactive is a free service — not a law firm — that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney who works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. We don't practice law or handle your case ourselves; we simply help you find someone who can look at what happened and explain your options. Reaching out costs you nothing and starts the process of getting real answers about your situation.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You Wait

items.title: Your filing window is limited
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim. If a government entity — like a city road crew or public bus — was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so acting sooner matters.

items.title: Being partly at fault doesn't shut you out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you shared some blame for the accident. Your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No cap on pain-and-suffering damages
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on non-economic damages such as pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life. This differs from some other states and can matter significantly in serious injury cases.

items.title: You don't pay unless there's a recovery
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so legal fees only come out of a settlement or award. There's no upfront cost to get a case evaluated.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Rancho Palos Verdes?
items.answer: Under California law, you generally have two years from the date of the injury to file a lawsuit. If your claim involves a government entity, such as a city-maintained road, that deadline can be much shorter — sometimes six months — so it's wise not to wait.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Rancho Palos Verdes?
items.answer: Public collision records show higher crash counts along corridors like Palos Verdes Drive S, Hawthorne Boulevard, and Western Avenue, with reports peaking on Monday afternoons between 2 and 4 p.m. These are simply reported patterns, not a judgment about any particular road or intersection.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, so partial fault reduces your compensation but doesn't prevent you from recovering it. An attorney can help evaluate how fault might be allocated in your specific situation.

items.question: Is there a cap on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: No — in typical personal injury cases, California does not cap non-economic damages like pain and suffering. Some exceptions apply in specific case types, such as medical malpractice, which an attorney can explain.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and we are not a law firm ourselves. Attorneys in the network work on contingency, so you pay nothing unless they recover compensation for you.
